claims.text: Combining machine learning on compositional and elemental features with ab initio molecular-dynamics calibration will improve prediction of low lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The integrated approach can capture enhanced phonon scattering caused by compositional disorder.
High-entropy alloys relevant to thermal insulation exhibit high configurational disorder across broad composition ranges.
The predictive framework will use a machine-learning algorithm trained on compositional and elemental-property data.
The machine-learning predictions will be calibrated using ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
Time-domain thermoreflectance measurements can provide the experimental lattice thermal conductivity values used to verify the predictions.
The approach will be evaluated over 300–700 K and across disordered alloy compositions relevant to thermal insulation.
Compositional disorder and associated local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering.
Heterogeneous atomic environments in high-entropy alloys produce significant force-constant fluctuations.
High-entropy-alloy atomic environments exhibit anharmonic effects that increase phonon scattering and reduce lattice thermal conductivity.
Machine-learning feature selection and simulation calibration will capture the disorder-related scattering mechanism.
Capturing compositional effects will improve prediction accuracy relative to models that neglect them.
The integrated predictions will be approximately 20% closer to TDTR measurements than predictions from conventional models.
The largest prediction improvement will occur in the low-lattice-thermal-conductivity regime.
The comparator consists of standard ab initio or Boltzmann-transport models that do not integrate detailed compositional features and scattering mechanisms.
The approach will be most applicable to compositionally complex high-entropy alloys and may not apply to ordered or low-entropy materials.
Prediction accuracy may decrease at extreme compositions or temperatures where additional nonlinear anharmonic effects dominate.
Failure to achieve predictions within 20% of measured values, or failure to statistically outperform conventional models, will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines improvement as predictions being approximately 20% closer than conventional-model predictions, whereas the falsification rule instead imposes an absolute 20% error margin against experiment. These are different performance criteria, so a result could satisfy one and fail the other.
